reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 20. Nay or No: 20. Not Voting: 0. Of 40 Yea or Nay votes where the Democratic majority could be computed, 38 (95%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 207 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

running.label: Candidates who filed with the FEC for this seat. Filing is not the same as being on the ballot. Primary results and ballot access are not shown.

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.
donor_industry.cycle_rule: House filings use the 2026 two-year cycle.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–323 of 2026 (323 votes, January 6, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.
stands_for.factual_flag: Not yet summarized: this line is built only from the official vote question and the bill's official title.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

posts.text: I voted to impeach Pete Hegseth for violating the Constitution, endangering civilian lives, and undermining our heroes in uniform. No one is above the law, and our service members deserve leadership worthy of their sacrifice. https://t.co/AMZAHDmwPg

This Veterans Day, we honor the Bronx veterans and military families who have given so much in service to our country.

They come from every walk of life, faith, and background, but share a commitment to something greater than themselves.

To all who have served, thank you. We are forever grateful.

The Bronx is mourning the tragic loss of 15 year old Javits Frimpong. I am standing with his family and community during this unimaginable time. I’m urging the U.S. Embassy in Ghana to expedite his mother’s visa, and we will work with the State Department to help bring her to New https://t.co/syIPIxZZ5h

I am devastated to learn that the fire at the Patterson Houses that took 11-year-old Zion Maine’s life on Wednesday has now claimed three more members of his family, including two teenage boys. My deepest condolences go to everyone who loved them and to the Patterson community, which is now mourning four lives. I am praying for Zion’s father as he recovers.

This tragedy makes the need for a mandatory federal safety standard for e-bike and scooter batteries even more urgent. My bill to create one passed the House last year, and the Senate cannot keep waiting while families pay the price.

My office remains here for the family and for the residents of 320 Morris Ave.

Yesterday morning, 15-year-old Javits Frimpong was shot and killed near Crotona Park on his way to school. Javits came to the Bronx from Ghana just a year ago to join his father and begin a new life here. Our entire borough is mourning a young man who should have had his whole https://t.co/rKvCV8jRa2

I am heartbroken by the death of a boy in an overnight fire at the Patterson Houses. My deepest condolences go to his family and to the entire Patterson community, who are grieving with them. I am praying for the four others who remain in critical condition.

The FDNY has https://t.co/6mEMxfVzd7

I joined @MSNOWNews's @ahylton26 and longtime Bronx advocate Joseph McManus to call for Aleksander Nilaj's release from ICE detention. For over a decade, Aleks has fed Bronx families through his food pantry, @AaohaFoodPantry. His case shows the human cost of an immigration system that tears families apart. We need him home.

Earlier this month, Pal-Awda boasted about forcing a Jewish community event out of Queens. Now the group has set its sights on Riverdale, targeting Jewish families in our borough simply for gathering together. Riverdale is home to one of the most vibrant Jewish communities in New https://t.co/A7TJn99hlY

I am deeply disturbed by the outbreak of violence against protesters in Albania. The actions taken by the Albanian police are beyond the pale, and must end. Albanians have a right to peacefully protest, the police must respect the protesters right to protest, and the police must https://t.co/83Blr3ceL3

Earlier today, my Bronx district office received an envelope delivered by mail that contained a suspicious substance. Local law enforcement responded swiftly and, after investigating, determined the substance to be non-hazardous. The evidence will now be sent to the FBI for further investigation. I’m grateful to the officers and first responders who acted so quickly to keep my staff and constituents safe.

“Families in the Bronx and across the country save up to buy these games, and they deserve better than a license that can vanish at any time. The Power To The Players Act ensures consumers own what they buy and can keep playing long after a company moves on.”

Read more below: https://t.co/67QKXj7abZ

I am outraged by the ICE shooting of a man in Marble Hill today as he sat in his car beside a 5-year-old child.

Firing multiple rounds into a car with a child inside, on a busy residential street in the Bronx, is abhorrent and indefensible. It put an entire neighborhood in danger and left a man seriously injured.

ICE has long operated as a rogue agency, and today’s shooting is a chilling reminder of how little regard it has for the safety of New Yorkers. I am calling on the DHS Inspector General to open an immediate and independent investigation, and on ICE to release all footage of the shooting. 

New Yorkers are owed a full accounting, not silence.

SNAP helps nearly 3 million New Yorkers afford groceries. Today, the federal share of SNAP administrative costs falls from 50% to 25%, shifting more costs to New York. I'm fighting to delay Trump's next SNAP cost shift and protect this critical lifeline. https://t.co/rCd9cR5nJb

Wishing a meaningful Yom Kippur to everyone observing in the Bronx and beyond. May this be a time for reflection, forgiveness, and connection with the people who matter most. G'mar Chatimah Tovah. https://t.co/tyDTWaxy2S

Electric bill too high? You may be eligible for a monthly discount.

New York State’s Energy Affordability Program can save you up to hundreds of dollars a year. This is on top of the $200 rebate checks going to millions of homes.

See if you’re eligible: https://t.co/6tr154xxKp https://t.co/KkkA1aR51b

Generaciones de neoyorquinos latinos han ayudado a forjar el Bronx que llamamos nuestro hogar.  

¡Feliz Mes de la Herencia Hispana! Sigamos celebrando nuestras culturas, tradiciones e historias, y construyendo juntos el futuro del Bronx. https://t.co/nvNJGqmwUK

Generations of Latino New Yorkers have helped shape the Bronx we call home.

This Hispanic Heritage Month, we celebrate our cultures, traditions, and histories.

Happy Hispanic Heritage Month! Let us continue to celebrate our roots and build the future of the Bronx together. https://t.co/UMtIUN7F6n

To our Jewish neighbors in the Bronx and beyond: wishing you and your loved ones a sweet and meaningful Rosh Hashanah.

May the new year bring health and happiness. Shana Tova! https://t.co/WWhY9WP0a3

The Legionnaires’ disease outbreak in Melrose and Morrisania is a serious matter for our community. My heart is with the Bronxites affected and their families. 

If you were in this area and develop flu-like symptoms, seek medical attention. Early treatment matters. 

Read my full statement below:

The NYC Health Department is investigating a cluster of Legionnaires' disease in Melrose and Morrisania. If you live, work, or recently visited the area and develop flu-like symptoms, please seek medical attention and follow the latest guidance. Learn more here: https://t.co/hWOedz5Q3Z

September 11 changed our city, our country, and countless lives forever.

Today, I remember every family who lost someone they loved, every survivor who carries the memories of that day, and every first responder who ran toward danger to save others.

We will never forget. https://t.co/PUWhF0lxzP
https://t.co/A93lZuusgL
https://t.co/AsqWRAG8aE

The Garífuna community is an important part of the Bronx, and this issue is deeply personal to many of my constituents. I'm urging Secretary Rubio and the State Department to press the Honduran government to protect Garífuna families and uphold their rights. https://t.co/FDH7L4S1Uh

Suicide prevention is personal to me. On World Suicide Prevention Day, I want to remind anyone struggling that you are not alone. There is help, there is hope, and you do not have to face it alone. Call or text 988 for support. https://t.co/gK7zMc1pQR

Happy Labor Day! Today, we celebrate everyone who shows up every day to work hard, care for their families, support their communities, and keep our city moving forward. Thank you for all that you do for the Bronx and beyond. https://t.co/nIQ0F3QKrM
Learn more and apply here: https://t.co/fq8YHt5Vv0

Calling all NY-15 students in grades 9-12! I’m proud to announce that our office is launching its first-ever Youth Advisory Council for the 2026-27 school year. Apply to learn about government, engage in public policy, and serve your community. Applications close Sept. 21. https://t.co/S3P0b0ol9o

My heart is with the Kingsbridge residents impacted by today's four-alarm fire. I'm grateful to the firefighters who worked through difficult conditions to contain the blaze and helped ensure that there were no serious injuries. 

My office is following the situation closely. Residents who need assistance can reach out to us or contact the Red Cross at 1-800-RED-CROSS.

For the first time in more than 100 years, a North American river otter has been spotted in the Bronx River!

This remarkable moment is a testament to decades of work by Bronx environmental activists and community leaders who fought to restore our river. We thank them for their dedication and celebrate this incredible milestone for the Bronx.
https://t.co/A8KEhiLwe1

A third person held at Delaney Hall, Jose Chajon-Raxon, has now died after ICE released him to a hospital.

ICE says it has no responsibility because he was no longer in custody.

That’s exactly the loophole our bill, the Families Deserve to Know Act, closes. ICE should not be able to release someone and then evade responsibility for what happens to them shortly after.

https://t.co/3JfcNWVdnl

My heart is with everyone in Colombia affected by yesterday’s devastating earthquake, and with the Colombian community here in the Bronx who are worried about their family back home. 

If you’re a constituent in NY-15 with loved ones impacted by the earthquake, our office is here to help.

For Americans currently in Colombia, please see below for important information and resources:

https://t.co/AJvtYIDa9y

Proud to join @GovKathyHochul in announcing a $9.7 million investment to complete a cardiac catheterization lab at @NYCHealthSystem/ Lincoln, bringing this kind of lifesaving emergency care to the Bronx for the first time. South Bronx families deserve critical care close to home, when every second counts.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
